messages.subject: Error in part4
parts:
Hello, 

I'm having some issues with part4, specifically integrating a sleeplog. 

When I include my sleeplog with the loglocation argument, I get the following error: 

Error in seq.int(0, to0 - from, by) : wrong sign in 'by' argument 
 
Otherwise, if I change it to loglocation = c(), then I get the following error: 

Error in pdf(file = paste0(metadatadir, "/results/visualisation_sleep.pdf")' : cannot open file "PATHWAY.pdf" 

I have tried overwriting the files and playing with the log itself. However, I haven't had any luck so far, and I can't seem to find the latter error in any previous discussions. I would appreciate any help! 

My code is as follows, and I have attached my sleeplog. 

g.shell.GGIR(mode = 1:5, datadir = "PATHWAY", outputdir = "PATHWAY", f0 = c(),f1 = c(), 
             overwrite = FALSE, do.report = c(2,4,5), visualreport = TRUE, 
             myfun = myfun, do.parallel = FALSE, #for step count 
             printsummary = TRUE, print.filename = TRUE,
             #PART 1
             windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600), #defining window
             desiredtz = "Australia/Adelaide", dynrange = 8, 
             do.enmo = TRUE, acc.metric = "ENMO", do.anglez = TRUE, use.temp = TRUE, 
             do.cal = TRUE, #auto-calibration
             spherecrit = 0.3, minloadcrit = 240, 
             #PART 2
             metadatadir = c(),
             strategy = 3, 
             ndayswindow = 21, 
             includedaycrit = 10,  
             idloc = 2, 
             do.imp = TRUE, 
             dayborder = 0, 
             iglevels = TRUE,
             #PART 3
             anglethreshold = 5,timethreshold = 5, 
             ignorenonwear = FALSE, 
             do.part3.pdf = TRUE,
             #PART 4,
             HASIB.algo = 'vanHees2015',
             relyonguider = TRUE,
             loglocation = "PATHWAY.csv",
             SleepwindowType = 'TimeInBed',
             nnights = 7, 
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE, 
             colid = 1,
             coln1 = 2,
             outliers.only = TRUE, 
             sleepefficiency.metric = 1,
             #PART 5,
             part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE, 
             frag.metric = 'all', 
             save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE, 
             save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE, 
             qwindow = c(0, 24), 
             excludefirstlast = FALSE, 
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutcriter.in = 0.9, boutcriter.lig = 0.8, 
             threshold.lig = c(44.8), threshold.mod = c(100.6), threshold.vig = c(428.8), 
             timewindow=c("MM"),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10), boutdur.in = c(10,20,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10)) 

Thanks in advance,

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part4
parts:
Hi Erin,

The code works well for me with the test file you sent, although I do not have the sleep diary but I doubt the sleep diary is the problem itself.

Please try:
  • Restart RStudio or do dev.off() a couple of times in the console to close the connection with the pdf file if it was still open until it shows null device. And delete existing pdf files.
  • If that does not work, retry in a new output locations such that all files have to be recreated.

On a differentent note I observed some minor things in your R script:
  • You do not need to see do.parallel = FALSE for step count. This was a mistake in their documentation which I think they corrected at some point.
  • metadatadir is not a GGIR parameter, you can leave it out. It is an internal parameter that you as GGIR user should not have to worry about.
  • You are setting a lot of parameter values to their defaults. There is no need to set parameters to their default value. It also does not do any harm except from making your R script longer.

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error in part4
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Thanks so much for the advice and sorry for the late reply. 

I've done some more investigating, and it seems that error is triggered by a subset of files within a larger batch. I've identified 5 files (out of 100), which trigger the error. It seems that these files have larger calibration errors than the other files (>0.025), although some of the 'successful' files also have similar calibration errors, so I'm not sure if this is the problem. Interestingly, when I run the batch of 5 'problem' files together, I'm able to get outputs as usual and no error is triggered. 

Now that I have found the issue, it's easy enough for us to operationalise a solution on our end! However, I wanted to update you so: 1) others can find this thread if they are having the same problem; and 2) you can implement changes to the code if needed. 

If you're interested in the latter, I can provide the meta files if that would be helpful. 

Best,
Erin
